glossary.Ascending aorta: First part of the aorta rising from the heart, before the arch.
glossary.Aortic arch: Curved part of the aorta giving off the head and arm arteries.
glossary.Descending aorta: Part of the aorta running down through the chest and abdomen after the arch.
glossary.Subclavian artery: Artery under the collarbone supplying the arm.
glossary.Connective tissue disorder: Inherited or acquired disease of the structural proteins that support tissues, such as collagen or fibrillin.
glossary.Aortic aneurysm: Permanent dilation of the aorta to at least 1.5 times normal diameter.
glossary.Mediastinum: Central chest compartment between the lungs containing the heart and great vessels.
glossary.Diastolic murmur: Abnormal heart sound heard between S2 and S1, while the heart relaxes.
glossary.Loin pain: Pain in the flank between the ribs and hip, often from the kidney.
glossary.Mesenteric: Relating to the arteries supplying the bowel.
glossary.Muffled heart sounds: Quiet heart sounds, as fluid around the heart dampens them.
glossary.Bibasal crackles: Crackles at both lung bases, typical of pulmonary oedema.
glossary.Peripheral oedema: Swelling of the legs or ankles from fluid in the tissues.
glossary.Cardiac failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Ischaemic ECG changes: ST or T wave changes showing the heart muscle is short of blood.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.Transoesophageal echocardiography: Heart ultrasound with the probe passed into the oesophagus, giving close views of the aorta.
glossary.Beta-blocker: Drug blocking beta-adrenoceptors to slow the heart and lower blood pressure.
glossary.Opioid: Strong painkiller acting on opioid receptors, e.g. morphine.
glossary.Morphine: Strong opioid painkiller given IV for severe pain.
glossary.Propagation: Extension of a tear or clot further along a vessel.
glossary.Proximal: Nearer the origin, here towards the heart.
glossary.Distal: Further from the origin, here away from the heart.
glossary.Aortic valve annulus: Fibrous ring that supports the aortic valve leaflets.
glossary.Myocardial ischaemia: Heart muscle short of oxygen from reduced coronary flow.
glossary.Pulsatile: Pumping in rhythm with the heartbeat.
glossary.STEMI: ST-elevation myocardial infarction: full-thickness heart attack seen on ECG.
glossary.Dissection flap: The torn inner layer of the aorta seen on imaging, separating true and false lumens.
